title: The Troubleshooting Methodology

header.html: 5.1 Explain the troubleshooting methodology: identify the problem; establish a theory of probable cause; test the theory to determine the cause; establish a plan of action and identify potential effects; implement the solution or escalate; verify full system functionality and implement preventive measures; document findings, actions, outcomes and lessons learned
the official CompTIA Network+ N10-009 exam objectives, version 4.0

html:
1The seven steps

# Step What you do
1 Identify the problem Gather information, question users, identify symptoms, determine whether anything has changed, duplicate the problem if possible, approach multiple problems individually
2 Establish a theory of probable cause Question the obvious; consider multiple approaches: top-to-bottom or bottom-to-top OSI, divide and conquer
3 Test the theory to determine the cause If confirmed, determine next steps; if not confirmed, establish a new theory or escalate
4 Establish a plan of action Plan the fix and identify potential effects (impact, rollback)
5 Implement the solution or escalate Make the change, or escalate if outside your authority or skill
6 Verify full system functionality and implement preventive measures Confirm the fix and that nothing else broke; prevent a repeat
7 Document findings, actions, outcomes and lessons learned Record everything, throughout the process
Exam tip

. Memorize the order. Testing the theory comes before the plan of action; documentation is last (and continues throughout).

2Approaches

Approach How it works
Top-to-bottom OSI Start at the application layer and work down
Bottom-to-top OSI Start at the physical layer (cables, link lights) and work up
Divide and conquer Start at the layer you suspect, then go up or down
Question the obvious Is it plugged in? Is the port enabled? Is the interface up?

3Practical habits

Habit Why
Ask what changed Most outages follow a change
Change one thing at a time You know what fixed it
Duplicate the problem Confirms the symptom and tests the fix
Escalate when needed Do not guess beyond your authority
Exam tip

. "Users report the issue after a weekend maintenance" = ask what changed first. Change one variable at a time.

Exam tip

. Test the theory before you plan the fix; document throughout and last.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A user cannot reach a file server. The technician asks the user what error appeared and whether anything changed recently. Which step is this?

  • AIdentify the problem
  • BEstablish a theory of probable cause
  • CTest the theory
  • DDocument findings
Show the answer

Answer: A. Gathering information and asking about changes is the first step.

S2After forming a theory, what should the technician do next?

  • AImplement the solution immediately
  • BDocument lessons learned
  • CVerify full functionality
  • DTest the theory to determine the cause
Show the answer

Answer: D. The theory must be tested before acting.

S3The technician's theory is not confirmed. What should be done next?

  • AImplement the original solution anyway
  • BEstablish a new theory or escalate
  • CClose the ticket
  • DReplace all cabling
Show the answer

Answer: B. If the theory fails, form a new one or escalate.

S4A technician starts at the physical layer by checking cables and link lights, then moves up. Which approach is this?

  • ABottom-to-top OSI
  • BTop-to-bottom OSI
  • CDivide and conquer
  • DQuestion the obvious only
Show the answer

Answer: A. Starting at layer 1 and moving up is bottom-to-top.

S5After the fix, the technician confirms users can work and checks that no other service broke. Which step is this?

  • AVerify full system functionality and implement preventive measures
  • BEstablish a plan of action
  • CIdentify the problem
  • DTest the theory
Show the answer

Answer: A. Verification follows implementation.

S6Which step happens throughout the process and also at the very end?

  • AEstablishing a theory
  • BEscalating
  • CDuplicating the problem
  • DDocumenting findings, actions and outcomes
Show the answer

Answer: D. Documentation continues from start to finish.

4.2 Recall questions

R1How many steps does the methodology have?

Show the answer

Seven.

R2What is the first step?

Show the answer

Identify the problem.

R3What is divide and conquer?

Show the answer

Starting at the layer you suspect and working up or down.

R4What should you determine about the environment first?

Show the answer

Whether anything has changed.

R5What comes after testing the theory when it is confirmed?

Show the answer

Determine the next steps and establish a plan of action.

R6What is the last step?

Show the answer

Document findings, actions, outcomes and lessons learned.

5Quick Reference Card

Step Key action
1 identify the problem (gather, question, symptoms, changes, duplicate)
2 theory of probable cause (obvious, OSI approaches, divide and conquer)
3 test the theory (confirmed or new theory or escalate)
4 plan of action with potential effects
5 implement or escalate
6 verify and prevent
7 document
